steps.title: Implement Stable Next-Token Loss
steps.action: Freeze a tiny token sample and implement numerically stable cross-entropy against a reference; use the environment prepared on Day0.
steps.evidence: Fixed sample manifest and matching loss values.

steps.title: Implement And Check Causal Attention
steps.action: Read the relevant A1 section, derive tensor shapes, and implement scaled causal attention with a future-token perturbation test.
steps.evidence: Documented shapes and a passing causal-independence test.

steps.title: Assemble Your First GPT Block
steps.action: Combine attention, learned positions, pre-norm and GELU components into a GPT-style block; rerun shape, causality and loss checks.
steps.evidence: GPT block passes shape, causality and stable-loss checks.

steps.title: Finish The Tiny GPT Model
steps.action: Assemble the tiny decoder and output head; verify dimensions and parameter count on the fixed sample.
steps.evidence: A complete decoder produces finite token logits.

steps.title: Implement A Verified Training Step
steps.action: Check a scalar or vector AdamW update by hand; add built-in AdamW, backward and gradient clipping.
steps.evidence: Hand calculation agrees with AdamW; training step reduces tiny-batch loss.

steps.title: Overfit And Sample Tiny Sequences
steps.action: Overfit a repeated tiny batch with dropout disabled; implement generation and save the short loss curve and samples.
steps.evidence: Tiny-batch loss meets its documented target; samples and curve saved.

steps.title: Save And Resume Model Training
steps.action: Checkpoint model, optimizer, schedule, RNG and data position; compare reload logits and resumed versus uninterrupted training.
steps.evidence: Reload reproduces logits; supported deterministic resume reproduces the training trajectory.

steps.title: Replace Normalization And Feedforward Layers
steps.action: Read relevant A2 sections and replace LayerNorm/GELU components with RMSNorm and SwiGLU; check shapes and finite gradients.
steps.evidence: RMSNorm and SwiGLU have documented shapes and passing smoke checks.

steps.title: Derive And Implement Rotary Positions
steps.action: Read A3, derive the rotary construction, and implement RoPE with explicit position offsets.
steps.evidence: Position-zero identity and relative-position dot-product tests pass.

steps.title: Implement Grouped Query Attention Heads
steps.action: Implement GQA with explicit query and KV head counts; compare output with an expanded-KV reference.
steps.evidence: Grouped heads match the expanded-KV reference.

steps.title: Validate The Modern Dense Decoder
steps.action: Integrate all four changes, rerun causality and tiny-batch checks, and document differences from exact Llama compatibility.
steps.evidence: Integrated decoder passes RoPE, GQA and causal correctness gates.

steps.title: Practice Functional JAX State Handling
steps.action: Read targeted A4 sections; exercise pytrees, explicit random keys and pure parameter/state updates on tiny arrays.
steps.evidence: Repeatable small examples show explicit parameters, state and random keys.

steps.title: Apply JAX Transformations To Primitives
steps.action: Use `grad`, `vmap` and `jit` on small layer calculations; inspect shapes and numerical outputs.
steps.evidence: Small transformation examples run with expected shapes and derivatives.

steps.title: Port Shared Decoder Layer Primitives
steps.action: Port normalization, rotary positions, projections and feedforward primitives; initialize both frameworks from shared NumPy arrays.
steps.evidence: Shared arrays produce matching primitive forward outputs.

steps.title: Verify Cross Framework Primitive Gradients
steps.action: Compare selected primitive gradients and outputs; resolve layout, epsilon and precision differences within declared tolerances.
steps.evidence: PyTorch and JAX primitive output and gradient parity table.

steps.title: Assemble The Functional JAX Decoder
steps.action: Connect the existing JAX primitives into the complete dense decoder with explicit parameter and RNG inputs.
steps.evidence: Complete decoder runs on the tiny configuration.

steps.title: Match Parameter Layouts Across Frameworks
steps.action: Define parameter conversion and transfer identical weights; compare intermediate activations and full logits.
steps.evidence: Shared weights yield matching full-model logits.

steps.title: Implement The Functional Training Step
steps.action: Add explicit optimizer state and a jitted training step; align loss reduction and optimizer semantics with PyTorch.
steps.evidence: Functional training state updates correctly without hidden mutation.

steps.title: Validate Full Model Numerical Parity
steps.action: Compare full logits, loss and representative parameter gradients on CPU FP32; document justified operation-specific tolerances.
steps.evidence: Full-model logits, loss and representative gradients satisfy the parity gate.

steps.title: Design And Implement KV Cache
steps.action: Add explicit per-layer KV state and position offsets to the PyTorch decoder, using tiny prompts for debugging.
steps.evidence: Incremental decoding updates cache shapes and offsets correctly.

steps.title: Verify Cached And Full Prefix Logits
steps.action: Compare cached next-token logits with full-prefix recomputation across several prompt lengths and nonzero offsets.
steps.evidence: Cache and full-prefix logits agree within stated tolerances.

steps.title: Freeze Data And Run Training Pilots
steps.action: Freeze the document split and shared token stream; launch bounded training pilots in PyTorch and JAX.
steps.evidence: Both frameworks complete short pilots using the frozen split.

steps.title: Measure Completed Training Work
steps.action: Build a synchronized throughput and memory report from the pilot; use it to calculate a bounded two-arm training allowance.
steps.evidence: Frozen data split, cache parity and initial throughput/memory ledger recorded.

steps.title: Derive And Implement Low Rank Updates
steps.action: Read A5 and implement LoRA for a linear layer with explicit rank, scaling and frozen base weights.
steps.evidence: Trainable parameters match the calculated low-rank count.

steps.title: Check Initialization And Merge Behavior
steps.action: Verify zero-update initialization and implement merging; compare merged and unmerged outputs with identical inputs.
steps.evidence: Initialization preserves the base; merged and unmerged outputs agree.

steps.title: Load The Small Pretrained Decoder
steps.action: Read A6; load SmolLM2-360M with its official tokenizer, pinned revision and documented configuration.
steps.evidence: Pinned pretrained model and tokenizer produce a baseline output.

steps.title: Integrate And Validate LoRA Adapters
steps.action: Attach adapters to selected linear layers; verify frozen base gradients, trainable count and merged/unmerged model logits.
steps.evidence: Base stays frozen; trainable count and merge-logit equivalence pass.

steps.title: Generate And Check Structured Data
steps.action: Generate 300 training, 50 validation and 100 held-out examples with separated template/entity families; manually spot-check labels.
steps.evidence: Split manifest and checked labels document family separation.

steps.title: Prepare Masked SFT And Baseline
steps.action: Build prompt-token masking and task graders; measure baseline syntax validity and task accuracy on the held-out set.
steps.evidence: Mask checks pass; baseline validity and accuracy saved.

steps.title: Run The Bounded Fine Tuning Experiment
steps.action: Train the LoRA adapters on the small structured task; inspect training and validation behavior and save the learning curve.
steps.evidence: Adapter checkpoint and training/validation curve recorded.

steps.title: Evaluate Structured Task Improvement Honestly
steps.action: Run the frozen held-out evaluation after SFT; compare validity and task accuracy, and document synthetic-data limitations.
steps.evidence: Before/after held-out metrics, learning curve and limitations recorded.

steps.title: Specify Sparse Expert Routing Shapes
steps.action: Read A7 selectively; define four experts, top-2 routing, tensor shapes and total versus active parameter counts.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned design and parameter accounting recorded.

steps.title: Implement The Explicit MoE Forward
steps.action: Implement the four-expert top-2 layer with explicit loops and weighted expert outputs on tiny tensors.
steps.evidence: Forward runs with documented routing and output shapes.

steps.title: Build A Dense Masked Reference
steps.action: Build the dense masked reference and compare forward outputs plus input and parameter gradients.
steps.evidence: MoE output and gradients match the reference.

steps.title: Inspect Routing And Validate Sparse Experts
steps.action: Log expert routing counts on ordinary and skewed inputs; rerun equality checks and explain utilization and active parameters.
steps.evidence: Reference equality passes; skewed routing and parameter accounting are visible.

steps.title: Trace MLA Projection Tensor Dimensions
steps.action: Read the relevant A8 equations and reference code; label projection, latent and positional tensor dimensions.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned MLA projection trace recorded.

steps.title: Follow Latent And Positional Cache State
steps.action: Trace what is cached for each generated token and how latent content and positional components contribute to attention.
steps.evidence: Cache-state walkthrough distinguishes content and position components.

steps.title: Compare MLA And GQA Memory
steps.action: Choose a concrete configuration and derive MLA and GQA cache bytes; distinguish cached state from model weights.
steps.evidence: Worked cache-memory comparison with explicit configuration and units.

steps.title: Explain Compression And MLA Differences
steps.action: Write the architecture note linking dimensions, cache equations and code; explain why a naive low-rank KV projection is insufficient.
steps.evidence: Architecture note includes dimensions, cache accounting and the naive-compression distinction.

steps.title: Read The Hybrid Attention Structure
steps.action: Read targeted A9 sections and identify recurrent and global-attention components in the hybrid design.
steps.evidence: Component map identifies recurrent state and global attention.

steps.title: Trace A Single Recurrent Update
steps.action: Follow one token through Gated DeltaNet equations or reference code, labeling every input and state dimension.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned one-token recurrence walkthrough recorded.

steps.title: Compare State And Cache Scaling
steps.action: Derive persistent recurrent-state storage and contrast it with growing KV storage at specified sequence lengths.
steps.evidence: Explicit state-versus-cache scaling comparison.

steps.title: Explain The Hybrid Design Tradeoffs
steps.action: Finish the dimensioned recurrence walkthrough and explain hybrid trade-offs, labeling any code trace separately; implement a tiny recurrence only if core work already passes.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned recurrence walkthrough and persistent-state comparison complete, with implementation depth labeled.

steps.title: Map Gemma Components Against Your Decoder
steps.action: Read relevant A10 sections and map attention, cache, routing and positional choices against the implemented dense model.
steps.evidence: Attributed Gemma component comparison with explicit knowledge depth.

steps.title: Map DeepSeek Components Against Your Decoder
steps.action: Read relevant A11 sections and add attention, cache, routing, position and training choices to the comparison.
steps.evidence: Attributed DeepSeek component comparison with explicit knowledge depth.

steps.title: Survey Post Training And Multimodal Interfaces
steps.action: Use targeted A1 material to survey DPO, GRPO and multimodal interfaces; connect each to its required inputs and objectives.
steps.evidence: Concise survey distinguishes objectives and interface changes.

steps.title: Specify A Matched Attention Comparison
steps.action: Define GQA and MHA configurations with the same model width, query-head count, head dimension, layers and token shapes; record changed K/V projection widths, parameter counts, precision and measurement protocol.
steps.evidence: Comparison configuration explicitly states shared settings and parameter differences.

steps.title: Validate Attention And Cache Accounting
steps.action: Run correctness checks for both configurations and calculate KV bytes at the chosen prompt lengths.
steps.evidence: Correctness gates pass and cache-byte calculations are recorded.

steps.title: Measure Prefill And Decode Separately
steps.action: Run synchronized inference measurements with controlled inputs and warm-up, reporting prefill separately from cached decode.
steps.evidence: Raw prefill/decode timings and hardware settings saved.

steps.title: Interpret The GQA Versus MHA Study
steps.action: Summarize cache bytes and inference timings; discuss parameter differences and explain why these measurements establish no quality equivalence.
steps.evidence: Matched study reports correctness, memory, prefill, decode and qualified conclusions.

steps.title: Build a Controlled Training Experiment
steps.action: Create executable baseline and ablation configurations, verify hard stopping conditions and test the launcher on a tiny fixture.
steps.evidence: Baseline and ablation differ in one declared choice.

steps.title: Run And Inspect The Baseline
steps.action: Finish the bounded baseline at the model size and token allowance supported by your pilot; inspect checkpoints and collect training/validation curves within that frozen budget.
steps.evidence: Baseline checkpoint and curves record exact consumed tokens.

steps.title: Run The Matched Training Ablation
steps.action: Finish the ablation using matched data order and token budget; collect comparable curves and sample generations.
steps.evidence: Ablation results retain matched data order and token budget.

steps.title: Compare Curves And State Limitations
steps.action: Compare baseline and ablation curves and samples; record exact token counts, configuration and limits of the available seeds.
steps.evidence: Training/validation curves, samples, token budget and seed limitations documented.

steps.title: Automate Tiny Training and Numerical Parity
steps.action: Implement one executable command that produces a fresh tiny training curve and shared-weight PyTorch/JAX parity results.
steps.evidence: An executable reproduction command writes fresh training/parity outputs with source and configuration metadata.

steps.title: Test Reproduction Failure Handling
steps.action: Inject missing input, invalid configuration and a failed parity subprocess; make the reproduction command fail clearly, then restore and run the valid path.
steps.evidence: Invalid-input and failed-child tests return nonzero status; the restored valid command regenerates fresh evidence.

steps.title: Prepare a Small Upstream Contribution
steps.action: Prepare a focused contribution for a real observed friction, or a verified compatibility note if no current upstream issue remains.
steps.evidence: A minimal reproducer and contribution draft, or a versioned compatibility/limitation note with runnable evidence.
